newsitem.title: INDIA: India's RBI buys dollars to arrest rupee's rise.
newsitem.headline: India's RBI buys dollars to arrest rupee's rise.

text.p: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) bought dollars on Thursday, the sixth successive trading day, in its bid to stall a strengthening rupee, dealers said.
"They bought at 35.70 level today also," said the chief dealer at a state-run bank in Bombay.
But dealers in several banks said they were not aware of RBI intervention on Thursday.
RBI stepped in after the rupee breached the 35.70-mark to trade briefly at 35.6975, dealers said.
The rupee closed Thursday at 35.6950/7025 against the dollar. The rupee had opened the day steady at 35.70/71.
The forex market is largely inactive on Friday as Bombay banks are closed for a Moslem holiday.
